sentences.text: 2. The case of the prosecution is that the family of the defacto complainant was residing near the house of the petitioners herein and the victim is closely associated with the family of the petitioners.

While she was pursuing her studies in college, her family shifted their residence and thereafter,
petitioners 1 and 2 herein met the victim's family to extend wedding invitation of the 3 rd petitioner herein and renewed their acquaintance.

In the month of January, 2019 the 1st accused/Arun Kumar had proposed his love towards the defacto complainant and on 14.05.2019 at 4.30 p.m, he taken the victim to the house of one Rajendran and had sexual intercourse with the victim on false promise of marriage, which was https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Crl.O.P.(MD).No.13876 of 2021 repeated.
Thereafter, he avoided her.
Therefore, the victim disclosed the said fact to the petitioners' family for which they advised her to avoid A1 citing the caste difference.
At that time, A1 came and slapped her and attempted to stab her.
After, she disclosed the affair to A1 and her family members, her father invited the petitioners for solution.

On 26.04.2020 at about 7.00 p.m. the petitioners arrived at the residence of the victim and supported their son which resulted to lodge the complaint before the All Women Police Station, Fort, Tiruchirappalli City on 02.05.2020, wherein A1 had appeared for enquiry and promised to marry her within three months, but he did not keep the said promise and on 22.01.2021 at about 4.15 p.m, while the victim was coming near Nagammal Temple, A1 waylaid her, abused her and assaulted her due to which the present complaint has been lodged.

To substantiate the same, the learned counsel submitted that the judgment in the case of [Manik Taneja and another v. State of Karnataka and another] reported in 2015 (7) SCC 423.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
constitute the offence under Section 506(i) of IPC, as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parminder Kaur v. State of Punjab,
reported in (2020) 8 SCC 811, no assault was made, which was the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Crl.O.P.(MD).No.13876 of 2021 material ingredient of Section 506 (i) of IPC.
In the case of Manik Taneja and another Vs. State of Karnataka and another reported in 2015 [7] SCC 423 Threat must be intention to cause alarm to the complainant to cause that person to do or omit to do any work.
Mere expressions of any words, without any intention to cause alarm would not be sufficient to bring in the application of this Section.
7.2.In the case of Noble Mohandass Vs. State, reported in 1988 [2] MWN Crl 184:
Threat should be a real one and not just a mere word when the person uttering it does exactly mean what he says and also when the person at whom thereat is launched does not feel threatened actually.
8. By applying the above principle, this Court finds no ingredients to constitute the offence under Section 506(i) of IPC.
Therefore, this Court finds merit in the contention of the petitioner that no offence is made out as against the petitioners under Section 506(i) of IPC and the continuation of the petitioners is abuse of process of law.
